# The Ostland Coast

*Pages PDF 29-34*

## **The Ostland Coast**
## **A Rugged and Wild Coastline Whose Rocky Cliffs Harbour Wreckers**
Whilst Nordlanders proudly associate themselves with the sea, the other province of the Empire that possesses a coastline, Ostland, barely registers the fact. Ostlanders are seen as resentful folk, staunchly Sigmarite in their attitudes and prone to feuds with their neighbours. It is a Nordland jest that Ostlanders are reluctant to take to the waves because it would prove to them that there are lands beyond the Empire. 

Hans-Hals von Tasseninck had barely been crowned Grand Prince when he declared war on Talabecland, claiming that agents from that province had assassinated his son. The fighting takes place largely between various noble households who nurse grievances dating back to the age of strife when Ulrican Talabecland and Sigmarite Ostland often fought wars. Whilst it is sporadic in its intensity, the conflict rumbles on. 

The Ostland coastline is rugged. Sheer cliffs rise from the seas. Rockfalls and landslides are common, and jagged rocks litter the shorelines. The eaves of the Forest of Shadows, haven to Beastmen and Goblin tribes, reach to the cliffsides. Those who make their homes by the sea are pressed between the harsh environment, Norse sea raiders, and monsters inland. 

Ostland also wants for good governance. The von Königswalds, who ruled the province for centuries, preferred to keep court in Altdorf rather than govern their fief. Their supporters claimed that toadying at the capital was to the benefit of Ostland, but their detractors noted the marked destitution of the province to show that whatever Imperial favour was being courted, it wasn’t helping the province. In 2502 IC Ostwald von Königswald was unmasked as a traitor, and since then the province has been ruled by the noble von Tasseninck family. But their rule has been a benighted one. 

The von Tasseninck’s are an old line, members of the family had sat on the provincial throne before the rise of the von Königswalds. However, they had never been considered to be particularly illustrious. 

When handguns began to proliferate in the armies of the Empire circa 2000 IC, Borys von Tasseninck refused to supply them to Ostland’s State Troops, claiming ‘their implementation would mean wasting perfectly good swords and spears’. These words have become proverbial, uttered every time an Ostlander wishes to decry out-oftouch aristocrats. 

The chances of Ostland making the best of its coasts is unlikely. However, the nobleman Oleg von Raukov has suggested that Ostland create its own Sea Lord, and even a Third Fleet (like most folk in the Empire, he has no idea of the potential naval might of Carroburg). He is concerned by the increasing number of Norse raids that have happened recently and is canny enough to realise that whilst the von Tassenincks wage war against Talabecland no help can be expected from Wolfenburg.

## **Salkalten**
Nestled by the Gulf of Kislev, next to the MiddenheimErengrad road, Salkalten struggles under the weight of its own founding. Anyone walking through the town will spy crumbling architectural façades, corroded statues, and other signs of faded glory which, in truth, never really existed. Jens-Pieter Riemanns persuaded Grand Prince Ivan von Königswald to pour money into expanding Salkalten’s harbour and beautifying the buildings to lure trade away from Marienburg in 2455 IC. When the promised influx of coin failed to appear, Salkalten returned to its previous indolence and the town’s people, with typical Ostlander thriftiness, tore up much of the decorative façade and statues to use for ballast. 

Still, Salkalten is not entirely forgotten. Some sailors view it as a useful, and cheap, supply stop. The town maintains logging camps in the Forest of Shadows, and most of its money comes from selling lumber and salted fish to those passing through. It is also favoured by the Sons of Manann, who maintain a barracks by the town’s central square, many preferring Salkalten’s relative comfort to the drafty quarters offered by nearby Odrall’s Watch. Most locals appreciate their presence, and the order finds many eager recruits among the young townsfolk. Others grumble that the knights are a disruptive rabble, drunk more often than not as they indulge in their shore leave. 

## **Custom and Practice**
Salkalten is ruled by Baron von Wolder, a savvy politician with a nose for where Ostland’s political winds are blowing. After a run-in with supposed cultists, Wolder grew zealous in rooting out Chaos and, though Salkalten is barely more than a speck on the map, remains convinced the Ruinous Powers are trying to infiltrate it. The dockside guards have strict instructions to search incoming ships for signs of mutation or malevolent workings. 

However, Wolder takes little interest in mundane smuggling. This lack of oversight is something the custom officers are not shy in exploiting, charging a small ‘unloading fee’ for anything they find. Strangely, this has given Salkalten a reputation as a good spot for smuggling — sure, you may need to pay a few bribes, but you’re unlikely to have your goods confiscated and your ship stolen from beneath your boots. 

## **The Quarantine Dock**
The Quarantine Dock was established away from Salkalten’s harbour, the then-ruler’s response to an unknown plague back when the town was first expanded. Though rotted and ill cared-for, the dock is still watched over by the joint efforts of Shallya’s priesthood and the Sons of Manann. The Shallyans go aboard any ship forced to dock there for a mandatory forty-day quarantine due to sickness, clad in protective leathers to care for the sailors. Meanwhile, the Sons of Manann make sure no one from the ships can reach shore, catching escapees with nets before they can bring their affliction onto land. 

## Love Sick
_The Bonny Marie_ has been at the Quarantine Dock for fifty days. The priests turn away any who come close, save those bringing food, and no one has appeared on the _Marie’s_ deck in days. Niklas, a local tailor, is worried. His wife was a sailor aboard that ship and the priests won’t tell him what’s become of her. He would give anything to know she’s alive. 

## **The Boyar’s Brew**
The Boyar’s Brew is a boisterous tavern by the docks which boasts the last decent kvas and ale south of Kislev. The owner, a good-natured Kislevite named Senja Semyenova, is well-loved by the northerners who pass through. She takes delight in gathering gossip, and her free hand with the drink ensures she gets to hear plenty. 

The place is shunned by locals, but when a sailor wishes for more than a life hauling fish, it’s to The Boyar’s Brew they go. The tavern is a good place to find hands used to the Sea of Claws’ harsh climate, and many captains stop here for this reason. 

## Gospodar Gossip
_‘That Kislevite woman with the white hair has bought three rounds for the entire house already. Says she’s some boyar’s daughter — and I’m the Tzarina herself! I bet the coin’s dodgy.’_ 

_‘I heard the baron’s been cosying up with Count von Raukov. The Tassenincks won’t like that, Raukov’s too popular already. Probably why three of their spies are drinking by the fire there.’_ 

THE OSTL AND COAST 

## **Here Be Monsters**
A dingy shop on the edge of Salkalten’s central square, Here Be Monsters is easy to spot by the carved sea serpent and sextant above its door. Anyone looking for a map is sure to find what they need among its dusty piles of parchment. However, while the maps are all of exquisite quality, it is the proprietor’s singular specialty which puts them in high demand: locating monster lairs. 

Erika Krämer once worked as a cartographer on expeditions organised by Imperial Zoological Garden of Altdorf. She found herself on an extensive sea voyage, hunting down the creatures which call the world’s oceans home, and made extensive notes on their habits and habitations. After retiring from the adventuring life and returning to her home town of Salkalten, Erika put her map-making talents to good use, plotting out wherever monsters are said to lurk. 

Such knowledge is invaluable for a captain looking to avoid the sea’s worst dangers. There are no shortage of terrifying creatures, and Erika’s maps may mean the difference between a profitable journey and a watery grave. She takes great pride in her reputation and, while she no longer sets out on research voyages herself, she regularly updates her maps to reflect sailors’ stories, marking out beastly migrations according to new sightings or incidents of missing vessels. It’s difficult to be accurate with such news, but Erika pays well for anyone willing to go and confirm the location of a monster’s lair. Those who get on the irascible cartographer’s bad side, however, may find the next map they purchase leading into the jaws of an uncaring leviathan. 

## Lair Sweet Lair
A few rough-looking Norsemen came by with tales of a creature near Varaland. However, they weren’t able to agree on quite what the creature is. Eager to find out, Erika is looking to hire some folks to go and report back on their findings. 

Upon arriving in Varaland, however, it turns out there is no monster. A small Skaeling settlement has been spreading the stories to discourage Empire raids, and they won’t be happy to have their secret revealed. 

## **’ Trusten S Ship-Shape Supplies**
Trusten’s Ship-Shape Supplies is an odd sight in the midst of Salkalten’s general decrepitude. Fresh paint and bright signs decorate its façade, tempting travellers in with promising bargains. Here, a sailor can buy anything required for even the longest of voyages, at very generous rates — well, Lionel Trusten thinks they’re generous. 

The fifth son of a minor noble family, Trusten decided to make his own fortune and prove himself more than the unwanted child of an unnoteworthy lineage. He spied opportunity in Salkalten and, with no more help than a loan from his mother, took ownership of a lumber yard and river barge. From these humble beginnings, Lionel hired every shipwright, cooper, tanner, and fisherman he could find. The result is a flourishing business, providing every conceivable supply needed for a sea voyage. Salted meats, timber for repairs, leather cloaks and warm clothes, Trustan undercut Salkalten’s meagre competition, offering prices few captains could pass up. At least, he used to. 

Lately, a series of misfortunes have been striking his business. His woodcutters are refusing to go into the forests, muttering about mutants in the region, while his fishermen no longer catch anything which isn’t hideously twisted. Trustan has been forced to do the unthinkable and raise his prices; as good as blood in the water for the rivals circling him. 

But Trustan didn’t get this far to let a little misfortune send it all crumbling into the sea. He will weather this, and come back stronger than ever, once his mother sees sense and gives him another loan. 

## Message in a Bottle
While perusing Trustan’s wares, the Characters find a small bottle hidden behind a shelf. Inside are thorns, hair, and herbs (crushed Spellwort). Upon showing him the bottle, Trustan’s face goes pale. He draws out three identical bottles, all found in his home. He thought he was just unlucky, but what if he’s actually cursed? 

If the Characters find whoever is responsible for hiding these bottles, he’ll be happy to work out a cut-price deal on any supplies they need. 

SEA OF CL AWS 

## **’ Odrall S Watch – Sons of Manann Chapter House**
The Sons of Manann maintain watch stations across the northern coast. However, Odrall’s Watch, the squat, circular tower perched atop the cliffs near Salkalten, is their true home and where this knightly order first began. 

According to their histories, Odrall the Devout, the legendary navigator of Marienburg, happened to be standing atop these cliffs when he saw a fishing boat struggling against ferocious waves. He ran to the nearest hamlet and roused the villagers to aid the beleaguered fishermen. All hands were saved, though Manann still claimed the boat. In thanks, Odrall had the watch tower built and dedicated it to the sea god, so even those caught in his wrath might know his mercy. 

Odrall’s Watch was initially attended by volunteers from Salkalten, who would take it in turns to watch out for sailors in danger. They would then set out in their rowboats, offering aid if they could, or bearing witness to the mariners’ deaths if they couldn’t. But the Sea of Claws holds more dangers than waves and rocks, and these volunteers soon changed their remit from saving lives to proactively defending them. Naming themselves the Sons of Manann, they became a militant order, guarding the coast from raiders, wreckers, and monsters. 

Odrall’s Watch has expanded since those early days. While the tower remains its most striking feature, a fortified hall, chart room, and boat house have been added, though most Sons of Manann prefer more comfortable quarters within nearby Salkalten. However, there are always some of the order stationed here and, should they spy any in need, a rider is sent to Salkalten, rousing all who would answer their god’s call. 

## Lose Your Head
By the tower stands a statue of Manann, hands outstretched towards the waiting sea. This shrine is watched over by the order’s grand admiral himself and most new initiates make their vows before it. However, when the grand admiral came to the shrine one morning, he found it beheaded, a Sigmarite amulet dangling from its hand. 

## **Wreck of** _la Giron_
A day’s sail north of Lossol Bay there lies a place where the sea remains unnaturally still. Few ships go there, unless forced by dire circumstance. Those sailors who do, come back with tales of finding themselves no longer sailing, but surrounded by lush, inviting grass, or seeing their loved ones beckoning beneath the waves. Despite the direst warnings, there will always be someone willing to step over the edge of the deck. However, they are not greeted by a peaceful meadow. Instead, as they sink, a wrecked ship peels free from the murk. All around, spilling from its broken belly like the guts of a great wounded creature, is a king’s ransom in gold. These are the remains of the cursed ship _La Giron_ . 

_La Giron_ was part of an Estalian treasure fleet, ferrying plunder from Lustria’s ruined temple cities back across the Great Ocean. On its final voyage, it carried an enormous burnished gold disc, taken from the top of a great ziggurat. This disc is ancient beyond reckoning. It had been placed atop the temple shortly after the coming of Chaos, a Greater Daemon of Slaanesh imprisoned within. Soon after setting sail, the Daemon’s whispers wormed their way into the crew’s dreams. 

There are no stories of how _La Giron_ sank, or how it came to be so far from Estalia, but the Daemon remains trapped inside the rotting hulk. Now, all its power is turned to luring people to itself. One day, it is sure, it will snare someone capable of freeing it. Until then, it takes what pleasure it can in dooming the less worthy. 

## Fisherman’s Friend
Jannick was gutting fish when suddenly gold coins began to spill from a mackerel’s distended entrails. The same was true for the next one. And the next one! As he readied his knife for the final fish, he heard a voice whispering, telling him where far more riches than these might be found. 

Sure it must be a blessing from Manann, Jannick has begun gathering as many people together as possible to cast more nets where the voice directed. 

THE OSTL AND COAST 

## **Schönfeld**
The Skeer, a collection of jagged rocks cutting through the waves west of Salkalten, have claimed many ships. Treacherous currents mean even sailors familiar with the waters spit overboard for Manann’s blessing as they approach. However, without these hazards the village of Schönfeld could not exist. A coastal hamlet with meagre anchorage, Schönfeld is a taciturn place, even by Ostlander standards. The people make their living from fishing, supplemented by salvaging anything the Skeer catch in their teeth. Such wrecks are so common that, when a ship is lost along the route, a messenger is often sent to Schönfeld, where they may find its figurehead added to the pile in the village centre. 

While Schönfeld owes the Skeer for shelter and sustenance, the rocks have proven a poor deterrent to raiders. The village does not warrant much protection from the lords of Ostland and is seen as a blessed place by Stromfels’s worshippers, making it a tempting target. The villagers have faced attacks time and again, raiders coming to claim the Wrecker’s bounty for their own. That the village remains at all is testament to the people’s tenacity. Most recently, a Sarl raiding party, led by the infamous Wulfrik, set part of the town ablaze before any resistance could be mustered. Schönfeld is therefore a scarred place, its villagers suspicious and cold towards outsiders. Only smugglers who have proven themselves trustworthy are liable to be met with anything more than sullen silence. 

Those engaged in illicit trade with Kislev find Schönfeld a potential alternative to Salkalten. Most people here understand a smattering of Gospodarinyi, holding a grudging respect for the people of that harsh land, and are often more welcoming to them than to those from more southerly regions. This, combined with Salkalten’s rising bribes and Schönfeld’s lack of guards, means more smugglers are finding the decrepit village worth a visit, especially those whose wares might earn them Baron von Wolder’s ire. While this has not helped Schönfeld’s carrion reputation, there are still few places where the followers of the Ruinous Powers are more hated. 

## Sink or Swim
The night before a salvage operation, the engineers found their diving bell sabotaged. This scared off their usual crew, leaving them in a desperate position. 

## **’ the Raider S Rest**
Iron cages hang near Schönfeld’s harbour. The locals call them The Raider’s Rest and they are rarely empty. Each one holds a raider, or someone suspected of aiding them, their piteous moans and shouted curses the first warning to those approaching Schönfeld by sea. Most villagers have learned to ignore the wretches trapped inside; it doesn’t do to be suspected of paying too much attention. However, there are always some who enjoy placing bets on how long each will last. 

## **Schunen and Sigirsdottir: Salvage Specialists**
You don’t need their garish sign to find Schunen and Sigirsdottir’s. Simply follow the bickering. 

These two engineers have worked together for years, perfecting their diving bell designs. Unfortunately, their funding dried up — unlike their patrons who tried the prototype. Unwilling to give up, they came to Schönfeld to work as salvage experts. With Schunen’s designs and Sigirsdottir’s metallurgy, they know their diving bell will take them places no one has ventured before. Regrettably, this may be true. 

## A Storm God’s Hunger
A stick-thin man rattles his cage, begging to be freed. Manann has spoken to him! There is a cave which holds Stromfels’s hunger. You must take him there, or all will be doomed! 

Asking about him reveals he was a priest of Manann, found hanging lanterns on the Skeer to guide raiders. 

## **The Diving Bell**
The Diving Bell is a metal capsule with three glass port holes. A trap door allows access to the water, and air is stored in weighted barrels. A faucet lets the occupants control the air flow, managing the pressure. 

|**Craft**|**Crew**|**TB**|**W**|**Depth**|**Traits**|
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
|Diving Bell|4|6|35|375 ft|Experimental (5)|

**Experimental:** For every hour in use, a **Challenging (+0) Trade (Engineering)** Test is required. For any doubles rolled on a failure, something breaks. This can happen up to the Trait’s rating before the craft stops working. 

## ## **Troll Country**
## **A Blasted Wasteland Infested with Monsters**
At first sight, the wide Troll Country is one of the bleakest landscapes imaginable. Grassy steppe to the south, scrubby tundra to the north, with only a few hill ranges and forests to break the monotony. Overshadowing the far north are the brutal mountain ranges of Norsca, the only blessing of which is to provide an imperfect impediment to the Chaos Wastes. 

However, the steppe grasses are long, and many different birds nest there, attracting rats and foxes. Reindeer graze lichens in the cruelly bitter winters, grasses in the short summers. Wolves prey on all that moves. When the snow melts for a few warm months, rare plants and valuable herbs put forth colourful blossoms, and insects buzz. 

Troll Country certainly lives up to its name, but there are other beasts besides. Shaggy-haired Beastmen fight and hunt here. Winds blowing through the northern peaks give rise to abominable wolves and bears; more bizarrely, cunning two-headed foxes and fortune-telling talking fish. Beyond these oddities are nature spirits, grim entities of snow and biting wind, tenacious Wood Spites, and elusive flower spirits of summer. 

Despite this diversity, Trolls dominate here, especially in the far north where Throgg, the Troll King, keeps his court. Fortunately, it’s unusual to meet more than three of them living together — as the Ungol proverb has it, _‘if you see four Trolls together, one of them is dinner’_ . 

Despite the inhospitable climate, a few Humans live here permanently. Most are Ungol, but there are also Gospodar, Sarl Norsemen, and even Kurgan. They are predominantly nomadic and tribal, setting camp only when the snow is too deep for travel. Otherwise, they keep on the move, in part following game herds, but mostly to avoid the other wildlife — the monsters. 

Unsurprisingly, Troll Slayers are common visitors, often accompanying foolhardy traders and other travellers on risky errands. Such adventurous fools are many and varied; few venture far beyond the coast, but this is often deep enough for them to experience the country’s bleakness and monstrous horrors. The seaboard is as much Troll Country as anywhere else, and the rocky coastline and salt marshes are consequently known as the Bile Lands.
